carousels.title: Chase Taps Business Deposits To Offer Mortgage Rate Discounts
carousels.cover_text: chase just opened jumbo rates to business cash
carousels.caption:
Banks are leveraging commercial deposits to dominate self-employed mortgage pricing. Chase is letting small-business owners combine commercial liquidity with personal accounts to secure lower interest rates. As a former underwriter, I know self-employed files are tough due to tax write-offs, but balance-sheet offsets change the game. Depositories are using deep liquidity to undercut nonbank pricing without sacrificing yield. Nonbanks must find creative asset-verification solutions or risk losing high-net-worth borrowers entirely.

#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #loanofficer #mortgagerates #realestateinvesting
carousels.hook: small business liquidity is now a mortgage rate lever.
carousels.what_happened_heading: chase expands relationship pricing to business deposits
carousels.what_happened: Chase is allowing over seven million small-business customers to count eligible commercial deposits toward mortgage interest rate discounts. Business owners can now aggregate balances across Chase and J.P. Morgan accounts to unlock lower pricing.

breakdown.heading: moving beyond personal deposit limits
breakdown.body: Traditional relationship pricing required personal liquidity, excluding high-earning business owners who keep capital in corporate accounts. This change treats corporate liquidity as personal strength.

breakdown.heading: what underwriters look for on deposit trails
breakdown.body: In underwriting, using business asset balances requires verifying operating liquidity so business stability is not compromised. You must prove funds are not earmarked for payroll or taxes.

breakdown.heading: nonbank lenders face liquidity pressure
breakdown.body: Nonbank originators cannot match bank balance-sheet plays that leverage deep commercial deposits. Depository banks are using balance sheet depth to capture prime self-employed borrowers.

breakdown.heading: targeting high net worth self-employed files
breakdown.body: Self-employed borrowers often struggle with tax-return income qualification. Allowing corporate cash to buy down mortgage rates gives depositories a massive conversion advantage on complex files.

carousels.my_take_heading: depository banks are redefining borrower retention
carousels.my_take: Banks are no longer competing on rate sheets; they are competing on balance sheet aggregation. If nonbanks do not partner with wealth managers, they will lose prime self-employed market share.
carousels.action_lo: Audit your database for self-employed clients with business deposits to structure relationship pricing options before bank competitors do.
carousels.action_realtor: Pitch business owner clients on depository rate discounts to help them preserve purchasing power without sacrificing operating capital.
carousels.cta_question: Can nonbank lenders survive without asset-based rate offsets in a high-rate market?

carousels.title: UAD 3.6 Appraisal Fees Climb $65, Early Data Shows Faster Production
carousels.cover_text: uad 3.6 appraisals cost more but speed up
carousels.caption:
Appraisal fees are climbing under the new UAD 3.6 report format, but turnaround times are actually improving. Clear Capital data shows an average $65 cost increase during the transition, but appraisers gain efficiency once onboarded. As a former underwriter, I can confirm that structured appraisal data cuts review friction and eliminates unnecessary condition requests. While no buyer likes higher fees, reducing closing timelines saves money on rate lock extensions and removes stress from purchase contracts.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/27w9ftye
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #homebuying #loanofficer #housingmarket
carousels.hook: higher appraisal fees are buying faster loan underwriting turn times.
carousels.what_happened_heading: appraisal fees rise under uad 3.6 standard
carousels.what_happened: Clear Capital reports an average $65 fee increase as the industry transitions to the new UAD 3.6 appraisal format. Despite higher upfront costs, early production data shows appraisers are completing reports faster once trained.

breakdown.heading: restructuring the appraisal data structure
breakdown.body: The Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) 3.6 redesigns report architecture, forcing appraisers to input more granular property data upfront. Initial learning curves drive short-term cost increases.

breakdown.heading: underwriter efficiency on standardized reports
breakdown.body: For underwriters, standardized digital appraisal data cuts review times dramatically. Fewer ambiguous condition notes mean fewer appraisal conditions and faster clear-to-close decisions on files.

breakdown.heading: upfront cost vs pipeline velocity
breakdown.body: A $65 fee increase hurts borrower closing costs, but gaining days in turnaround speed prevents rate lock extensions. Pipeline velocity saves lenders more money than the fee costs.

breakdown.heading: preparing borrowers for higher fee sheets
breakdown.body: Loan officers must adjust Fee Worksheets and Loan Estimates early to reflect updated appraisal pricing. Discrepancies between estimates and actual appraisal invoices trigger tolerance cures.

carousels.my_take: Paying $65 more for an appraisal is a bargain if it removes three days of underwriter back-and-forth. Speed to close is worth more than minor fee savings.
carousels.action_lo: Update your fee templates now to avoid LE fee tolerances while appraisers adjust to new UAD pricing.
carousels.action_realtor: Set expectations with buyers that property appraisal fees are rising slightly, but faster turn times protect lock expiration dates.
carousels.cta_question: Is a $65 increase in closing costs worth saving two days in appraisal turn time?

carousels.title: Mortgage Credit Availability Declines Slightly in September
carousels.cover_text: lenders tighten credit on investors and cash outs
carousels.caption:
Mortgage credit availability dipped in September as lenders quietly trimmed risk in cash-out refinances and investor loans. Core primary purchase guidelines remain intact, but peripheral loan products are seeing stricter overlays. From my years in underwriting, when rate volatility stays high, secondary investors demand larger cushions on non-owner occupied debt. Loan officers must double-check borrower reserves and cash-flow ratios on investment deals now to prevent unexpected file rejections before closing.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/274s2e7d
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #housingmarket #realestateinvesting #loanofficer
carousels.hook: mortgage credit availability pulled back again as lenders reduce exposure.
carousels.what_happened_heading: mortgage credit index falls in september
carousels.what_happened: Mortgage credit availability declined slightly in September according to industry metrics. Lenders specifically pulled back on product offerings for cash-out refinances and investor property purchases.

breakdown.heading: targeting high risk product categories
breakdown.body: Credit pullbacks were concentrated in investor loans and cash-out refinances rather than primary purchase programs. Lenders are trimming peripheral risk while defending core agency business.

breakdown.heading: what underwriters see on investor files
breakdown.body: In underwriting, cash-out and investor files face stricter reserve requirements and tighter debt-service coverage metrics. Higher interest rates make investor cash-flow calculations fail faster.

breakdown.heading: liquidity restrictions impact non agency space
breakdown.body: Secondary market appetite for non-agency investor paper is shrinking as capital providers demand higher risk premiums. Nonbank lenders are forced to narrow their product menus.

breakdown.heading: purchase money focus stays intact
breakdown.body: While cash-out and investor guidelines tighten, owner-occupied purchase programs remain fully accessible. Lenders are allocating balance sheet capacity strictly to primary home buyers.

carousels.my_take_heading: lenders are quietly de-risking before year end
carousels.my_take: This is not a housing crash; it is secondary market risk discipline. Investors without strong cash reserves will find fewer debt options as lenders protect balance sheets.
carousels.action_lo: Re-underwrite investor pre-approvals today to ensure their cash flow and reserve requirements still meet updated guidelines.
carousels.action_realtor: Advise investor clients to secure financing pre-approvals with non-QM or portfolio lenders before making cash-out purchase offers.

carousels_es.hook: la liquidez de pequeños negocios es ahora clave para tu tasa hipotecaria.

breakdown.heading: enfocándose en trabajadores independientes de alto patrimonio

carousels_es.title: Disminuye ligeramente la disponibilidad de crédito hipotecario en septiembre

carousels_es.caption:

Los prestamistas deben verificar de nuevo las reservas del prestatario y los ratios de flujo de efectivo en acuerdos de inversión ahora para evitar rechazos inesperados antes del cierre.
